## Day 016 · lang-cpp — Abstract classes, pure virtual functions, and vtables

Source: [`days/day-016-2d-arrays/07-lang-cpp-abstract-classes-pure-virtual.md`](../../days/day-016-2d-arrays/07-lang-cpp-abstract-classes-pure-virtual.md)

- A pure virtual operation defines required behaviour.
- Derived classes implement that behaviour.
- Base references preserve virtual dispatch.
- override catches signature mistakes.
- An owning polymorphic base needs appropriate destruction.

## Day 016 · lang-go — Interfaces are satisfied implicitly; the empty interface; io.Reader

Source: [`days/day-016-2d-arrays/06-lang-go-interfaces-are-satisfied-implicitly.md`](../../days/day-016-2d-arrays/06-lang-go-interfaces-are-satisfied-implicitly.md)

- An interface lists required methods.
- Concrete types satisfy it implicitly.
- Assignment checks the method set at compile time.
- Pointer and value method sets differ.
- A typed nil inside an interface is not a nil interface.

## Day 016 · lang-python — Duck typing, abstract base classes, and Protocol

Source: [`days/day-016-2d-arrays/05-lang-python-duck-typing-abstract-base.md`](../../days/day-016-2d-arrays/05-lang-python-duck-typing-abstract-base.md)

- Duck typing asks whether an object supports an operation.
- Protocol describes that shape to static checkers.
- Ordinary annotations do not enforce it at runtime.
- ABC can prevent construction of incomplete subclasses.
- A matching method name does not prove correct behaviour.

## Day 017 · lang-cpp — Public inheritance, virtual, override, and object slicing

Source: [`days/day-017-matrix-tricks/07-lang-cpp-public-inheritance-virtual-override.md`](../../days/day-017-matrix-tricks/07-lang-cpp-public-inheritance-virtual-override.md)

- Public inheritance commits to the base's contract.
- Virtual dispatch follows the dynamic object.
- Base references preserve the derived object.
- Copying into a base value slices derived state.
- Composition often makes replaceable parts easier to reason about.

## Day 017 · lang-go — Struct embedding, and why Go has no inheritance

Source: [`days/day-017-matrix-tricks/06-lang-go-struct-embedding-and-why.md`](../../days/day-017-matrix-tricks/06-lang-go-struct-embedding-and-why.md)

- Go composition stores another value in a struct.
- Embedding can promote methods and fields.
- Promotion does not make the outer type a subtype.
- Interfaces express interchangeable behaviour.
- Use explicit delegation when it makes call paths clearer.

## Day 017 · lang-python — Inheritance, super(), and the MRO

Source: [`days/day-017-matrix-tricks/05-lang-python-inheritance-super-and-the.md`](../../days/day-017-matrix-tricks/05-lang-python-inheritance-super-and-the.md)

- Inheritance should preserve the base contract.
- Composition stores a collaborator with a separate job.
- Python resolves inherited attributes using the MRO.
- super continues lookup along that order.
- Choose reuse that preserves behaviour, not just fewer lines.

## Day 018 · lang-cpp — Templates, template argument deduction, and instantiation

Source: [`days/day-018-arrays-revision/07-lang-cpp-templates-template-argument-deduction.md`](../../days/day-018-arrays-revision/07-lang-cpp-templates-template-argument-deduction.md)

- Templates describe implementations parameterised by types.
- Instantiation checks the required operations.
- Stack<int> keeps an integer element contract.
- Make template definitions visible to instantiating code.
- Specify failure and evaluation order as carefully as in non-template code.

## Day 018 · lang-go — Type parameters, constraints, and any versus comparable

Source: [`days/day-018-arrays-revision/06-lang-go-type-parameters-constraints-and.md`](../../days/day-018-arrays-revision/06-lang-go-type-parameters-constraints-and.md)

- Type parameters make one implementation work for several types.
- Constraints determine permitted operations.
- any supports storage; comparable permits equality.
- Instantiation preserves each stack's element type.
- Separate empty-pop status from the zero value.

Further reading: [Go's generics tutorial](https://go.dev/doc/tutorial/generics).

## Day 018 · lang-python — typing generics: TypeVar, Generic, and list[T]

Source: [`days/day-018-arrays-revision/05-lang-python-typing-generics-typevar-generic.md`](../../days/day-018-arrays-revision/05-lang-python-typing-generics-typevar-generic.md)

- TypeVar names a relationship between input and output types.
- Generic[T] carries that relationship through a class.
- Static checkers preserve the concrete element type.
- Runtime Python does not enforce ordinary annotations.
- Specify empty-container behaviour independently.

## Day 019 · lang-cpp — Lambdas, capture lists by value and by reference, std::function

Source: [`days/day-019-what-a-string-is/07-lang-cpp-lambdas-capture-lists-by.md`](../../days/day-019-what-a-string-is/07-lang-cpp-lambdas-capture-lists-by.md)

- Lambdas are callable objects with captured state.
- Value capture stores a copy in the closure.
- Reference capture depends on the original lifetime.
- auto preserves the closure type; std::function wraps callables.
- Never return a closure referring to a destroyed local.

## Day 019 · lang-go — Function literals, captured loop variables, and function types

Source: [`days/day-019-what-a-string-is/06-lang-go-function-literals-captured-loop.md`](../../days/day-019-what-a-string-is/06-lang-go-function-literals-captured-loop.md)

- A function value preserves its parameter and result types.
- Closures share captured variables.
- Separate factory calls can retain separate state.
- Loop declarations and assignments have different capture consequences.
- Check the module language version when reasoning about loop variables.

The [Go 1.22 release notes](https://go.dev/doc/go1.22#language) document the per-iteration loop-variable change.

## Day 019 · lang-python — Functions as values, lambda, and captured variables

Source: [`days/day-019-what-a-string-is/05-lang-python-functions-as-values-lambda.md`](../../days/day-019-what-a-string-is/05-lang-python-functions-as-values-lambda.md)

- Functions can be returned and stored as values.
- A closure retains access to enclosing bindings.
- Captured bindings can be looked up at call time.
- Default arguments can take creation-time values.
- Use nonlocal for intentional enclosing rebinding.

## Day 020 · lang-cpp — Iterator categories, begin/end, and C++20 ranges

Source: [`days/day-020-building-strings/07-lang-cpp-iterator-categories-begin-end.md`](../../days/day-020-building-strings/07-lang-cpp-iterator-categories-begin-end.md)

- begin starts traversal; end marks its boundary.
- Iterator categories determine supported operations.
- Views compose lazy traversal without intermediate vectors.
- Borrowed sources must outlive their views.
- Laziness is not caching and does not guarantee less total work.

## Day 020 · lang-go — Range-over-func iterators (iter.Seq) and channels as iterators

Source: [`days/day-020-building-strings/06-lang-go-range-over-func-iterators.md`](../../days/day-020-building-strings/06-lang-go-range-over-func-iterators.md)

- Go 1.23 supports range over iterator functions.
- iter.Seq passes values to a yield callback.
- Return as soon as yield reports false.
- A channel producer needs explicit cancellation when consumers stop.
- Repeatability depends on the iterator's state and design.

Further reading: [Go's range-over-functions explanation](https://go.dev/blog/range-functions).

## Day 020 · lang-python — __iter__, __next__, yield, and generator expressions

Source: [`days/day-020-building-strings/05-lang-python-iter-next-yield-and.md`](../../days/day-020-building-strings/05-lang-python-iter-next-yield-and.md)

- An iterable supplies an iterator.
- An iterator advances with next until StopIteration.
- yield suspends a generator with its local state.
- Exhausted generators do not restart themselves.
- Streaming saves storage only if consumers avoid materialising everything.
